examples.text: Hoy he llegado 20 minutos antes a la estación de tren.
examples.trans: Today I arrived at the train station 20 minutes early.

examples.text: El autobús número 20 para justo delante del mercado central.
examples.trans: Bus number 20 stops right in front of the central market.

meanings.note: Cardinal number written in digits and read in Spanish as veinte (/ˈbejnte/); invariable for gender.

examples.text: Mi hermano mayor cumple 25 años el próximo sábado.
examples.trans: My older brother turns 25 years old next Saturday.

examples.text: La entrada al museo tiene descuento para menores de 25 años.
examples.trans: Museum admission has a discount for visitors under 25 years old.

meanings.note: Cardinal number written in digits and read in Spanish as veinticinco (/bejntiˈθiŋko/), spelled as a single compound word.
Marks destination, clock time, and animate direct objects (personal a).

examples.text: Vamos a la estación ahora.
examples.trans: We are going to the station now.

examples.text: El desayuno empieza a las ocho.
examples.trans: Breakfast starts at eight o'clock.

examples.text: Aakif trabaja como ingeniero informático en el centro de Madrid.
examples.trans: Aakif works as a computer engineer in central Madrid.

examples.text: Hoy hemos quedado con Aakif para tomar un café cerca del parque.
examples.trans: Today we arranged to meet Aakif for a coffee near the park.

meanings.note: Romanization of the Arabic given name Akif, meaning 'devoted' or 'steadfast'.
Indicates position or movement downward.

examples.text: La cocina está abajo.
examples.trans: The kitchen is downstairs.

examples.text: Te espero abajo en el patio.
examples.trans: I will wait for you downstairs in the courtyard.

examples.text: Por favor, los viajeros deben abandonar el vagón por la puerta delantera.
examples.trans: Please, passengers must exit the carriage through the front door.

examples.text: Decidió no abandonar sus estudios de piano a pesar del cansancio.
examples.trans: He decided not to give up his piano studies despite being tired.

meanings.note: More formal than dejar or irse when vacating a room, building, or vehicle.

meanings.en: to abandon; to give up on
meanings.note: Used for quitting a habit, course of study, or race.
Refers both to the white-barked birch tree and its pale, smooth wood (madera de abedul).

examples.text: Estas pinzas de madera de abedul tienen una superficie muy lisa.
examples.trans: These birch-wood clothespins have a very smooth surface.

examples.text: En el norte crecen bosques enteros de abedules blancos.
examples.trans: Whole forests of white birch trees grow in the north.

meanings.note: Often seen in plural compounds such as cera de abejas ('beeswax') and miel de abejas ('bee honey').

examples.text: Una abeja se posó en la flor del limonero.
examples.trans: A bee landed on the lemon tree blossom.

examples.text: La tela está cubierta con cera pura de abejas.
examples.trans: The cloth is coated with pure beeswax.

meanings.note: Used literally or figuratively (ablandarse, to soften up).

examples.text: El vapor ablanda la madera.
examples.trans: Steam softens the wood.

examples.text: Con una sonrisa siempre se ablanda.
examples.trans: With a smile he always softens up.

meanings.note: A legal professional (feminine: la abogada).

examples.text: El abogado está aquí.
examples.trans: The lawyer is here.

examples.text: Vemos los abogados desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the lawyers from the door.

examples.text: La doctora Abouk pasa consulta en el hospital general los jueves.
examples.trans: Doctor Abouk sees patients at the general hospital on Thursdays.

examples.text: Hemos enviado la invitación de la cena a la familia Abouk.
examples.trans: We sent the dinner invitation to the Abouk family.

meanings.note: Family surname of Maghrebi Arabic origin attested in Spain and Tunisia.
Describes clothing, blankets, or rooms that keep out the cold.

examples.text: Es una pieza abrigada.
examples.trans: It is a warm piece.

examples.text: Tengo una manta abrigada, así que esta noche estoy muy cómodo.
examples.trans: I have a warm blanket, so tonight I am very comfortable.

meanings.note: Warm outer coat worn in cold or rainy weather.

examples.text: El abrigo está aquí.
examples.trans: The coat is here.

examples.text: Vemos los abrigos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the coats from the door.

meanings.note: Months of the year are lowercase and masculine in Spanish.

examples.text: En abril llueve a menudo.
examples.trans: In April it often rains.

examples.text: Llegaron a la ciudad en abril.
examples.trans: They arrived in the city in April.

meanings.note: Regular -ir verb with irregular past participle abierto.

examples.text: Abro la ventana por la mañana.
examples.trans: I open the window in the morning.

examples.text: Ayer abrimos la tienda temprano.
examples.trans: Yesterday we opened the shop early.

meanings.note: In en absoluto, means 'not at all'.

examples.text: Hay un silencio absoluto aquí.
examples.trans: There is complete silence here.

examples.text: No me molesta en absoluto.
examples.trans: It does not bother me at all.

meanings.note: Describes non-figurative art (pintura abstracta) or theoretical ideas.

examples.text: La pintura abstracta al agua queda preciosa en la pared del café.
examples.trans: The abstract watercolour painting looks lovely on the café wall.

examples.text: Prefiero los ejemplos prácticos a las ideas demasiado abstractas.
examples.trans: I prefer practical examples to overly abstract ideas.

meanings.note: Feminine counterpart of abuelo.

examples.text: Mi abuela amasaba pan casero todos los domingos.
examples.trans: My grandmother kneaded homemade bread every Sunday.

examples.text: Guardamos la receta de limón de nuestra abuela.
examples.trans: We keep our grandmother's lemon recipe.

meanings.note: Plural los abuelos also means 'grandparents'.

examples.text: El abuelo está aquí.
examples.trans: The grandfather is here.

examples.text: Vemos los abuelos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the grandfathers from the door.

meanings.note: Meaning shifts between ser (boring) and estar (bored).

examples.text: Este documento es muy aburrido.
examples.trans: This document is very boring.

examples.text: Hoy no estoy nada aburrido.
examples.trans: Today I am not bored at all.

examples.text: Las conferencias demasiado largas suelen aburrir al público.
examples.trans: Overly long lectures usually bore the audience.

examples.text: Siempre llevo una novela en la mochila para no aburrirme en el tren.
examples.trans: I always carry a novel in my backpack so I do not get bored on the train.

meanings.note: Transitive use when a book, talk, or routine bores someone.
Very frequent pronominal form: aburrirse como una ostra ('to be bored stiff').
Past-participle adjective from acabar (una mesa bien acabada).
Used with estar for exhaustion or ruin.

examples.text: Es una pieza de madera muy bien acabada.
examples.trans: It is a very well-finished wooden piece.

examples.text: Después de caminar veinte kilómetros, estamos acabados.
examples.trans: After walking twenty kilometers, we are worn out.

acabar.gloss: to finish; to have just (acabar de)

meanings.en: to finish; to have just (acabar de)
meanings.note: Acabar de + infinitive means 'to have just done something'.

examples.text: Acabo de llegar del mercado.
examples.trans: I have just arrived from the market.

examples.text: Ya acabamos el trabajo de hoy.
examples.trans: We already finished today's work.

examples.text: Acabo de preparar café recién hecho en la cocina.
examples.trans: I have just made fresh coffee in the kitchen.

examples.text: En cuanto acabo el trabajo los viernes, doy un paseo largo por el río.
examples.trans: As soon as I finish work on Fridays, I take a long walk by the river.

meanings.note: 1st-person singular present of acabar; used in the periphrasis acabar de + infinitive for an action completed moments ago.
Used standalone for completing work or with a gerund (acabo cansado / acabo haciéndolo).

related.gloss: to finish; to have just (with de)

acaso.gloss: perhaps; by chance (por si acaso = just in case)

meanings.en: perhaps; by chance (por si acaso = just in case)
meanings.note: Most common in everyday speech inside the fixed phrase por si acaso ('just in case').

examples.text: Llevo un paraguas pequeño por si acaso llueve.
examples.trans: I carry a small umbrella just in case it rains.

examples.text: Horneamos otra bandeja de pan por si acaso vienen más vecinos.
examples.trans: We baked another tray of bread just in case more neighbours come.

meanings.note: Por accidente means 'by accident'.

examples.text: El accidente está aquí.
examples.trans: The accident is here.

examples.text: Vemos los accidentes desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the accidents from the door.

examples.text: Agradecemos mucho tu rápida acción para ayudar a los vecinos.
examples.trans: We really appreciate your quick action to help the neighbours.

examples.text: Prefiero las novelas de misterio con mucha acción y ritmo ágil.
examples.trans: I prefer mystery novels with plenty of action and a brisk pace.

meanings.note: Everyday feminine noun for physical movement, initiative, or a kind deed (una buena acción).
In economics, las acciones are shares in a company.
Used both for cooking oil (aceite de oliva) and lubricating oil on hinges.

examples.text: Pon dos gotas de aceite en la bisagra seca.
examples.trans: Put two drops of oil on the dry hinge.

examples.text: Aliñamos la sopa caliente con aceite de oliva.
examples.trans: We dress the hot soup with olive oil.

examples.text: Mi vecino habla español con un suave acento andaluz.
examples.trans: My neighbour speaks Spanish with a soft Andalusian accent.

examples.text: No olvides escribir el acento en la última sílaba de canción.
examples.trans: Do not forget to write the accent mark on the last syllable of canción.

meanings.note: Describes the characteristic melody and pronunciation of a region or speaker.
Refers both to prosodic word stress and the written acute accent mark.
Regular -ar verb.

examples.text: Aceptamos el presupuesto para arreglar la sala.
examples.trans: We accept the budget to fix the room.

examples.text: ¿Aceptan pago en efectivo en este puesto?
examples.trans: Do they accept cash payment at this stall?

meanings.note: Standard word in Spain for the pedestrian walkway beside a street.

examples.text: La acera está aquí.
examples.trans: The pavement is here.

examples.text: Vemos las aceras desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the pavements from the door.

acercar.gloss: to bring closer; to move closer

meanings.en: to bring closer; to move closer
meanings.note: Spelling changes c -> qu before -e (acerqué, acerque).

examples.text: Acerca la lámpara a la mesa de trabajo, por favor.
examples.trans: Bring the lamp closer to the workbench, please.

examples.text: Acercamos dos sillas de madera junto al piano.
examples.trans: We move two wooden chairs closer to the piano.

examples.text: La mesa pesa poco, así que podemos acercarla un poco más a la ventana.
examples.trans: The table weighs very little, so we can move it a bit closer to the window.

examples.text: Como llovía tanto, me ofrecí a acercarla en coche hasta la estación.
examples.trans: Since it was raining so hard, I offered to give her a lift to the station.

meanings.en: to move it closer; to bring her closer
meanings.note: Infinitive acercar fused with the feminine singular direct-object clitic la (referring to a feminine noun like la silla or la lámpara, or to a female person).

meanings.en: to give her a lift; to drop her off nearby
meanings.note: In Peninsular Spanish, acercar a alguien means to give someone a short ride toward their destination.
Strong metal alloy used in piano strings, tools, and kitchenware.

examples.text: Las cuerdas agudas del piano son de acero fino.
examples.trans: The high piano strings are made of thin steel.

examples.text: Guarda los tornillos de acero en esta caja pequeña.
examples.trans: Keep the steel screws in this small box.

meanings.note: Spelling changes g -> j before o (acojo).

examples.text: El patio acoge a muchos vecinos.
examples.trans: The courtyard welcomes many neighbours.

examples.text: La casa nos acogió con cariño.
examples.trans: The house hosted us warmly.

meanings.note: Takes personal a before a person (acompañar a Carmen); also used for musical accompaniment (con el violín).

examples.text: Te acompaño hasta la parada del autobús.
examples.trans: I will walk with you to the bus stop.

examples.text: El vecino acompaña a la pianista con su violín.
examples.trans: The neighbour accompanies the pianist on his violin.

examples.text: ¿Te acuerdas del nombre de aquella panadería tan buena del centro?
examples.trans: Do you remember the name of that really good bakery downtown?

examples.text: Los vecinos acordaron pintar la escalera del edificio en primavera.
examples.trans: The neighbours agreed to paint the building's staircase in spring.

meanings.en: to remember; to recall (pronominal acordarse de)
meanings.note: Stem-changing verb (o -> ue) taking the preposition de when pronominal: me acuerdo de todo.

meanings.en: to agree on; to set (transitive acordar)
meanings.note: Without a reflexive pronoun, acordar means to reach an agreement (acordar una fecha).
Used with de for what you remember: me acuerdo de esta lámpara. Stem o changes to ue.

examples.text: ¿Te acuerdas de mi nombre?
examples.trans: Do you remember my name?

examples.text: No me acuerdo de dónde está la llave.
examples.trans: I don't remember where the key is.

meanings.note: Several musical notes played together.

examples.text: Toca un acorde muy suave.
examples.trans: She plays a very soft chord.

examples.text: Este acorde suena triste.
examples.trans: This chord sounds sad.

examples.text: En clase de inglés aprendimos que la palabra 'action' significa acción.
examples.trans: In English class we learned that the word 'action' means action.

examples.text: El profesor escribió 'action' en la pizarra para practicar la pronunciación.
examples.trans: The teacher wrote 'action' on the board to practice pronunciation.

meanings.note: English word encountered by Spanish learners in language classes, games, and film terminology; the native Spanish equivalent is acción.

examples.text: Ese joven actor estudió arte dramático en una escuela de Córdoba.
examples.trans: That young actor studied drama at a school in Córdoba.

examples.text: Los actores saludaron al público desde el centro del teatro municipal.
examples.trans: The actors bowed to the audience from the center of the municipal theatre.

meanings.note: Masculine noun; its feminine counterpart is la actriz (plural las actrices).

examples.text: Las dos actrices principales recibieron un largo aplauso en el teatro.
examples.trans: The two lead actresses received a long round of applause at the theatre.

examples.text: Varias actrices del grupo universitario ensayan en el salón de actos.
examples.trans: Several actresses from the university troupe rehearse in the auditorium.

meanings.note: Plural of la actriz; following standard Spanish spelling rules, final -z changes to -c- before -es.

examples.text: Mi prima mayor trabaja como actriz de teatro clásico en Sevilla.
examples.trans: My older cousin works as a classical theatre actress in Seville.

examples.text: La actriz agradeció el cariño de todos los asistentes al coloquio.
examples.trans: The actress thanked everyone attending the talk for their warmth.

meanings.note: Feminine counterpart of el actor; forms its plural as las actrices.

examples.text: El director actual de la biblioteca lleva tres años en el puesto.
examples.trans: The current director of the library has been in the post for three years.

examples.text: En la situación económica actual conviene ahorrar un poco cada mes.
examples.trans: In the current economic situation it is wise to save a little every month.

meanings.note: False friend: in Spanish, actual means 'current' or 'present-day', NEVER English 'actual' ('real, exact', which is real or verdadero).
Takes a written accent on ú in singular and 3rd plural present (actúo, actúa).

examples.text: Siempre actúa con mucha calma.
examples.trans: She always acts very calmly.

examples.text: Los músicos actúan el sábado en la plaza.
examples.trans: The musicians perform in the square on Saturday.

meanings.note: Refers both to the water-soluble paint medium (pintar a la acuarela) and to a finished watercolour painting.

examples.text: Javier pintó el patio con tinta y acuarela.
examples.trans: Javier painted the courtyard in ink and watercolour.

examples.text: Colgamos dos acuarelas pequeñas junto a la ventana.
examples.trans: We hung two small watercolours beside the window.

acudir.gloss: to attend; to show up; to keep (an appointment)

meanings.en: to attend; to show up; to keep (an appointment)
meanings.note: Followed by the preposition a before the place or appointment (acudir a una cita).

examples.text: Los pájaros acuden a la fuente cada mañana.
examples.trans: The birds come to the fountain every morning.

examples.text: Todos los vecinos acudieron a la apertura del café.
examples.trans: All the neighbours showed up for the café opening.

examples.text: En realidad soy arquitecto acústico y diseño auditorios de música.
examples.trans: Actually, I am an acoustic architect and I design music auditoriums.

examples.text: Pusieron paneles de aislamiento acústico en las paredes del estudio.
examples.trans: They installed acoustic insulation panels on the studio walls.

meanings.note: Relating to sound, room acoustics, or unamplified musical instruments (guitarra acústica).

examples.text: Van a adaptar la antigua estación de tren para hacer un museo local.
examples.trans: They are going to adapt the old train station to create a local museum.

examples.text: El menú del comedor está adaptado para personas con alergias alimentarias.
examples.trans: The dining-hall menu is adapted for people with food allergies.

meanings.note: Used transitively for modifying a text, space, or schedule to suit new needs; participle adaptado/a means 'adapted'.

meanings.en: to adjust; to settle in (reflexive adaptarse a)
meanings.note: Pronominal adaptarse a means getting used to a new city, climate, or routine.
Warm invitation to enter a room or proceed.

examples.text: ¡Adelante, la puerta está abierta!
examples.trans: Come in, the door is open!

examples.text: Adelante, puede sentarse aquí.
examples.trans: Go right ahead, you may sit here.

examples.text: Ha conseguido adelgazar cuatro kilos caminando una hora cada mañana.
examples.trans: He managed to lose four kilos by walking an hour every morning.

examples.text: Con tanto nadar en el mar este verano he adelgazado bastante.
examples.trans: With so much swimming in the sea this summer I have lost quite a bit of weight.

adelgazar.gloss: to lose weight; to slim down

meanings.en: to lose weight; to make thinner
meanings.note: Built on delgado ('thin, slender'); spelled with -c- before -e in forms like adelgacé.
Además de + noun means 'in addition to / besides'.

examples.text: Compramos limones y, además, dos tarros de miel.
examples.trans: We bought lemons and, in addition, two jars of honey.

examples.text: La sala es luminosa y además muy silenciosa.
examples.trans: The room is bright and also very quiet.

meanings.note: Regular -ar verb.

examples.text: ¿Puedes adivinar quién llamó hoy?
examples.trans: Can you guess who called today?

examples.text: Adivinó la respuesta enseguida.
examples.trans: She guessed the answer right away.

meanings.note: Standard farewell across the Spanish-speaking world.

examples.text: ¡Adiós y buen viaje!
examples.trans: Goodbye and have a good trip!

examples.text: Dijo adiós desde la puerta.
examples.trans: She said goodbye from the doorway.

meanings.note: Regular -ar verb meaning to look at with wonder or respect.

examples.text: Los vecinos se detuvieron en el patio para admirar los farolillos.
examples.trans: The neighbours stopped in the courtyard to admire the lanterns.

examples.text: Admiro mucho la paciencia con la que Mateo arregla cada reloj.
examples.trans: I greatly admire the patience with which Mateo fixes every clock.

meanings.note: Plural adoquines: traditional paving stones in historic streets.

examples.text: El adoquín está aquí.
examples.trans: The cobblestone is here.

examples.text: Vemos los adoquines desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the cobblestones from the door.

meanings.note: Expresses strong fondness in everyday speech.

examples.text: Adoro el olor a café recién hecho.
examples.trans: I adore the smell of freshly brewed coffee.

examples.text: Mis abuelos adoran este jardín.
examples.trans: My grandparents adore this garden.

examples.text: ¿Adónde vais de excursión este puente de mayo?
examples.trans: Where are you all going on a trip this May long weekend?

examples.text: Todavía no hemos decidido adónde iremos de vacaciones en agosto.
examples.trans: We still have not decided where we will go on holiday in August.

meanings.note: Used with verbs of motion (ir, viajar, llevar) in direct and indirect questions; written with a tilde when interrogative.

examples.text: El metro llega directamente a la terminal principal del aeropuerto.
examples.trans: The metro goes straight to the main airport terminal.

examples.text: Salimos con tiempo de casa para facturar las maletas en el aeropuerto.
examples.trans: We left home early to check our suitcases at the airport.

meanings.note: Compound masculine noun (aero- + puerto).
Denotes a favourite pastime or keen interest, as well as the devoted fans of an art or sport.

examples.text: La acuarela es la nueva afición de Clara los domingos por la tarde.
examples.trans: Watercolour painting is Clara's new hobby on Sunday afternoons.

examples.text: Mis dos vecinos comparten la misma afición por la música de piano.
examples.trans: My two neighbours share the same fondness for piano music.

meanings.note: Used for pencils with a fine point (lápiz afilado) as well as knives and tools.

examples.text: Mateo siempre lleva un lápiz bien afilado en el bolsillo del taller.
examples.trans: Mateo always carries a well-sharpened pencil in his workshop pocket.

examples.text: Ten cuidado con ese cuchillo de cocina porque está muy afilado.
examples.trans: Be careful with that kitchen knife because it is very sharp.

meanings.note: Regular -ar verb; llave de afinar is a piano tuning wrench.

examples.text: Carmen afina el piano de madera antes del viernes.
examples.trans: Carmen tunes the wooden piano before Friday.

examples.text: Afinamos cada cuerda con mucha paciencia y silencio.
examples.trans: We tune every string with great patience and quiet.

meanings.note: Opposite of apretar (to tighten).

examples.text: Aflojo el tornillo con cuidado.
examples.trans: I loosen the screw carefully.

examples.text: El mecánico aflojó la tuerca vieja.
examples.trans: The mechanic loosened the old nut.

agarrar.gloss: to grip; to stick; to take hold

meanings.en: to grip; to stick; to take hold
meanings.note: Said of paint or glue adhering to dry wood, as well as gripping with the hand.

examples.text: La pintura nueva agarra muy bien sobre madera seca.
examples.trans: Fresh paint sticks very well on dry wood.

examples.text: Agarra fuerte el otro extremo de la mesa.
examples.trans: Grip the other end of the table firmly.

examples.text: Siempre me agarro bien a la barra cuando el autobús frena de golpe.
examples.trans: I always hold on tight to the handrail when the bus brakes suddenly.

examples.text: Agarro el paraguas antes de salir porque el cielo está muy gris.
examples.trans: I grab my umbrella before heading out because the sky is very grey.

agarro.gloss: I grab; I hold on to

meanings.en: I grab; I grip; I catch
meanings.note: 1st-person singular present indicative of agarrar; completely neutral in Peninsular Spanish for holding firmly or grabbing an umbrella or bag.
Agencia de viajes = travel agency.

examples.text: Reservamos el billete en una agencia de viajes.
examples.trans: We booked the ticket at a travel agency.

examples.text: Hay varias agencias abiertas en esta avenida.
examples.trans: There are several branch offices open on this avenue.

examples.text: Déjame apuntar la fecha de la reunión en mi agenda de papel.
examples.trans: Let me write down the meeting date in my paper planner.

examples.text: Este mes el médico tiene la agenda completa hasta el próximo lunes.
examples.trans: This month the doctor's schedule is booked solid until next Monday.

meanings.note: In Spanish, una agenda is primarily a personal calendar or organizer where appointments and phone numbers are written down.
Refers to a day's planned commitments (tener la agenda llena) or the order of business.

examples.text: Estoy un poco agobiado con tantos exámenes finales esta semana.
examples.trans: I am a bit overwhelmed with so many final exams this week.

examples.text: Con el calor de julio se sintió agobiada dentro del vagón lleno.
examples.trans: In the July heat she felt stifled inside the crowded carriage.

meanings.note: High-frequency Peninsular adjective (used with estar) for feeling mentally swamped by tasks or physically stifled by heat or crowds.

examples.text: Mi hermano se agobió al ver la cola tan larga en la ventanilla.
examples.trans: My brother got overwhelmed when he saw such a long queue at the counter.

examples.text: El ruido constante de las obras nos agobió durante toda la mañana.
examples.trans: The constant noise from the roadworks stressed us out all morning long.

meanings.en: got overwhelmed; panicked under pressure (with se)
meanings.note: 3rd-person singular preterite of agobiar / agobiarse.
Transitive use when noise, heat, or excessive work overwhelms someone.
Same form for masculine and feminine.

examples.text: Es una pieza agradable.
examples.trans: It is a pleasant piece.

examples.text: Tranquilo y agradable, gracias, aunque esta maleta pesa mucho hoy.
examples.trans: Quiet and pleasant, thank you, though this suitcase weighs a lot today.

meanings.note: Feminine noun that takes el in the singular before stressed initial /a/ (el agua fría).

examples.text: Quiero un vaso de agua fría.
examples.trans: I want a glass of cold water.

examples.text: El agua de la ducha sale caliente.
examples.trans: The shower water comes out hot.

examples.text: Con estas botas de montaña puedo aguantar horas caminando bajo la lluvia.
examples.trans: With these hiking boots I can last hours walking in the rain.

examples.text: Casi no pudimos aguantar la risa cuando el perro nos robó el bocadillo.
examples.trans: We could barely hold back our laughter when the dog stole our sandwich.

aguantar.gloss: to put up with; to hold out; to endure

meanings.en: to bear; to put up with; to stand
meanings.note: Very common everyday verb in Spain: no aguanto el frío ('I can't stand the cold').

meanings.en: to hold back; to last; to hold up
meanings.note: Used for holding one's breath or laughter (aguantar la risa) or batteries/shoes lasting well.
Covers a sewing needle (aguja de coser), the hands of a clock (las agujas del reloj), and a magnetic compass needle.

examples.text: La aguja de acero azul apunta siempre hacia el norte.
examples.trans: The blued steel needle always points north.

examples.text: Busqué hilo y una aguja fina para coser el botón.
examples.trans: I looked for thread and a fine needle to sew the button.

meanings.note: Covers everything from tiny screw holes in wood to holes in clothing or walls.

examples.text: Hay dos agujeros pequeños para los tornillos en la madera.
examples.trans: There are two small screw holes in the wood.

examples.text: El perro cavó un agujero junto al árbol del jardín.
examples.trans: The dog dug a hole beside the garden tree.

meanings.note: Expresses sudden realization or understanding.

examples.text: ¡Ah, ya entiendo el mapa!
examples.trans: Ah, now I understand the map!

examples.text: ¿Ah, sí? Qué buena noticia.
examples.trans: Oh really? What good news.

meanings.note: Ahora mismo means 'right now'.

examples.text: Voy para allá ahora mismo.
examples.trans: I am heading there right now.

examples.text: Ahora tenemos cuatro mesas libres.
examples.trans: Now we have four free tables.

meanings.note: Points to something at medium distance or near the listener.

examples.text: Deja las llaves ahí en la mesa.
examples.trans: Leave the keys there on the table.

examples.text: Ahí viene el autobús.
examples.trans: There comes the bus.

meanings.note: Al aire libre means 'outdoors'.

examples.text: El aire es muy importante aquí.
examples.trans: The air is very important here.

examples.text: Hablamos sobre el aire.
examples.trans: We talk about the air.

meanings.note: Same form for masculine and feminine singular; cinta aislante is 'electrical tape'.

examples.text: Necesito un rollo de cinta aislante negra.
examples.trans: I need a roll of black electrical tape.

examples.text: El cristal grueso es un buen material aislante.
examples.trans: Thick glass is a good insulating material.

examples.text: Sofreímos dos dientes de ajo laminados en aceite de oliva virgen.
examples.trans: We gently fry two sliced cloves of garlic in virgin olive oil.

examples.text: En invierno apetece mucho tomar una sopa castellana con pan y ajo.
examples.trans: In winter a Castilian soup with bread and garlic really hits the spot.

meanings.en: garlic; clove or bulb of garlic
meanings.note: Countable in Spanish: un diente de ajo ('a clove of garlic'), una cabeza de ajos ('a head of garlic').
Exclamation of discovery or agreement.

examples.text: ¡Ajá, aquí estaban mis gafas!
examples.trans: Aha, here were my glasses!

examples.text: Ajá, eso explica el ruido.
examples.trans: Aha, that explains the noise.

meanings.note: Mandatory contraction of preposition a + masculine article el; al + infinitive means 'upon doing'.

examples.text: Vamos al mercado por la mañana.
examples.trans: We go to the market in the morning.

examples.text: Al abrir la puerta, sonó el timbre.
examples.trans: Upon opening the door, the bell rang.

examples.text: ¡Ala, qué nevada tan bonita ha caído esta noche en la sierra!
examples.trans: Wow, what a lovely snowfall fell last night in the mountains!

examples.text: ¡Ala, recoge los cuadernos de la mesa que ya nos vamos!
examples.trans: Come on, gather the notebooks off the table, we are heading out now!

meanings.en: come on!; wow!; goodness! (colloquial variant spelling of ¡hala!)
meanings.note: Informal Peninsular exclamation expressing surprise, encouragement, or brisk dismissal.

meanings.en: wing; brim of a hat (as feminine noun el ala / las alas)
meanings.note: Note that as a feminine noun beginning with stressed /ˈa/, it takes el in the singular (el ala izquierda, las dos alas).
Metal wire used for hanging lanterns or repairs.

examples.text: El alambre está aquí.
examples.trans: The wire is here.

examples.text: Vemos los alambres desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the wires from the door.

meanings.note: Feminine noun taking el in the singular before stressed a- (el alba, al alba).

examples.text: Rocío enciende el horno de la cocina al alba.
examples.trans: Rocio lights the kitchen oven at dawn.

examples.text: El patio huele a azahar fresco desde el alba.
examples.trans: The courtyard smells of fresh orange blossom from daybreak.

examples.text: Hoy en el mercado hemos comprado un kilo de alcachofas tiernas.
examples.trans: Today at the market we bought a kilo of tender artichokes.

examples.text: Las alcachofas salteadas con jamón son un plato delicioso de invierno.
examples.trans: Artichokes sautéed with ham are a delicious winter dish.

meanings.note: Classic winter and spring vegetable of Spanish market gardens (from Andalusi Arabic al-kharshūfa).
In Peninsular Spanish household vocabulary, la alcachofa also names the perforated head of a shower.

alegrar.gloss: to make glad; to cheer up

meanings.en: to make glad; to cheer up
meanings.note: Me alegra / nos alegra means 'it makes me/us glad'.

examples.text: Esa noticia nos alegra mucho.
examples.trans: That news makes us very glad.

examples.text: Las flores alegran toda la mesa.
examples.trans: The flowers brighten up the whole table.

meanings.note: Same singular form for masculine and feminine.

examples.text: El vals empieza con un ritmo ligero y alegre.
examples.trans: The waltz begins with a light, cheerful rhythm.

examples.text: Los colores alegres dan mucha vida al patio.
examples.trans: Cheerful colours bring lots of life to the courtyard.

examples.text: ¡Cuánto me alegro por ti al saber que aprobaste el examen práctico!
examples.trans: How glad I am for you on hearing that you passed the practical exam!

examples.text: Me alegro muchísimo de que hayáis encontrado un piso luminoso.
examples.trans: I am so happy that you all found a bright flat.

alegro.gloss: I am glad (with me); I brighten up

meanings.en: I am glad; I am happy (pronominal me alegro de)
meanings.note: 1st-person singular present of alegrarse; takes de before a noun, infinitive, or que-clause (me alegro mucho por ti).
Transitive sense: alegrar la casa con flores.

examples.text: ¡Qué alegría encontrarte por casualidad en esta cafetería!
examples.trans: What a joy to run into you by chance at this café!

examples.text: La visita inesperada de los nietos llenó toda la casa de alegría.
examples.trans: The grandchildren's unexpected visit filled the whole house with joy.

meanings.note: Everyday noun used in warm greetings such as ¡Qué alegría verte! ('What a joy to see you!').

alejar.gloss: to move away; to step back (alejarse)

meanings.en: to move away; to step back (alejarse)
meanings.note: From lejos ('far'); reflexive alejarse means 'to step back / move further away'.

examples.text: Aléjate dos pasos para ver el cartel entero.
examples.trans: Step back two paces to see the whole sign.

examples.text: Alejamos las tazas limpias del borde de la mesa.
examples.trans: We move the clean cups away from the edge of the table.

examples.text: Los diccionarios de la estantería están colocados por orden alfabético.
examples.trans: The dictionaries on the shelf are arranged in alphabetical order.

examples.text: El profesor pasó lista siguiendo el índice alfabético de apellidos.
examples.trans: The teacher called the roll following the alphabetical index of surnames.

meanings.note: Most commonly heard in the phrase por orden alfabético ('in alphabetical order').
From Hispanic Arabic al-ḥánbal.

examples.text: La alfombra está aquí.
examples.trans: The rug is here.

examples.text: Vemos las alfombras desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the rugs from the door.

meanings.note: Traditional Spanish architectural noun for the flat stone or wooden ledge at the bottom of a window.

examples.text: Carmen dejó el libro verde sobre el alféizar de su ventana.
examples.trans: Carmen left the green book on her windowsill.

examples.text: En el alféizar hay dos macetas de flores rojas.
examples.trans: There are two pots of red flowers on the windowsill.

meanings.note: Indefinite pronoun used in statements and questions.

examples.text: ¿Necesita algo más de la cocina?
examples.trans: Do you need anything else from the kitchen?

examples.text: Hay algo dentro de la caja.
examples.trans: There is something inside the box.

meanings.note: Used with de to describe fabric or heavy art paper: una camisa de algodón, papel de algodón.

examples.text: Las sábanas blancas son de algodón fresco.
examples.trans: The white sheets are made of cool cotton.

examples.text: Dibujó el mapa sobre papel grueso de algodón.
examples.trans: He drew the map on heavy cotton paper.

meanings.note: Refers exclusively to people.

examples.text: Alguien acaba de llamar a la puerta.
examples.trans: Someone just knocked at the door.

examples.text: ¿Hay alguien en recepción?
examples.trans: Is anyone at the front desk?

meanings.note: Shortens to algún before masculine singular nouns (algún problema).

examples.text: ¿Tiene algún cartel en la puerta?
examples.trans: Does it have any sign on the door?

examples.text: Compré algunas manzanas rojas.
examples.trans: I bought some red apples.

examples.text: Nos sentamos un minuto en el banco de piedra para recuperar el aliento.
examples.trans: We sat down for a minute on the stone bench to catch our breath.

examples.text: Subió la cuesta en bicicleta y llegó al mirador casi sin aliento.
examples.trans: He rode his bicycle up the hill and reached the viewpoint nearly out of breath.

meanings.note: Used in expressions such as recuperar el aliento ('to catch one's breath') and sin aliento ('out of breath').
Figurative sense in palabras de aliento ('words of encouragement').

examples.text: Pedimos una ración de alitas de pollo asadas con limón para compartir.
examples.trans: We ordered a portion of lemon-roasted chicken wings to share.

examples.text: El gorrión movía una alita cerca de la fuente del jardín.
examples.trans: The sparrow was fluttering a little wing near the garden fountain.

meanings.en: little wing; chicken wing (especially plural alitas de pollo)
meanings.note: Diminutive of ala; in Spanish menus and tapas bars, las alitas refers to roasted or fried chicken wings.

examples.text: Se quedó mucho más aliviada cuando encontró las llaves dentro del abrigo.
examples.trans: She felt much more relieved when she found the keys inside her coat.

examples.text: Al conocer las buenas noticias del médico, respiró tranquila y aliviada.
examples.trans: Upon hearing the good news from the doctor, she breathed calmly and felt relieved.

meanings.note: Feminine singular of aliviado (from aliviar, 'to relieve, ease'), typically paired with estar or sentirse.
¡Qué alivio! means 'What a relief!'.

examples.text: El alivio es muy importante aquí.
examples.trans: The relief is very important here.

examples.text: Hablamos sobre el alivio.
examples.trans: We talk about the relief.

meanings.note: Allá va is a natural everyday phrase before flipping a switch or starting something.

examples.text: Allá va la primera prueba de la lámpara.
examples.trans: Here goes the first test of the lamp.

examples.text: Pon las sillas plegadas más allá del arco.
examples.trans: Put the folded chairs further past the arch.

meanings.note: Points to a place farther away from both speakers.

examples.text: La farmacia está allí en la esquina.
examples.trans: The pharmacy is over there on the corner.

examples.text: Vivimos allí durante seis años.
examples.trans: We lived there for six years.

meanings.note: Feminine noun taking el in the singular before stressed /a/ (el alma, las almas).

examples.text: El alma está aquí.
examples.trans: The soul is here.

examples.text: Vemos las almas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the souls from the door.

meanings.note: Plural almacenes.

examples.text: El almacén está aquí.
examples.trans: The storeroom is here.

examples.text: Vemos los almacenes desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the storerooms from the door.

meanings.note: Classic Mediterranean baking ingredient in tarts and biscuits.

examples.text: Rocío hornea galletas crujientes de almendra y limón.
examples.trans: Rocio bakes crunchy almond and lemon biscuits.

examples.text: Tostamos las almendras cinco minutos en el horno.
examples.trans: We toast the almonds for five minutes in the oven.

meanings.note: Soft bed pillow.

examples.text: La almohada está aquí.
examples.trans: The pillow is here.

examples.text: Vemos las almohadas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the pillows from the door.

meanings.note: Related to the verb almorzar ('to have lunch'); in parts of Spain (including Valencia) el almuerzo can also refer to a hearty mid-morning snack.

examples.text: Servimos el almuerzo en el patio a las dos.
examples.trans: We serve lunch in the courtyard at two o'clock.

examples.text: No me muevo de la recepción hasta la hora del almuerzo.
examples.trans: I am not moving from the front desk until lunchtime.

meanings.note: Used reflexively (alojarse) for staying at a hotel or inn.

examples.text: Muchos viajeros se alojan aquí.
examples.trans: Many travellers stay here.

examples.text: Nos alojamos en una casa tranquila.
examples.trans: We stayed at a quiet inn.

meanings.note: Covers both renting from a landlord and renting out to a guest.

examples.text: Alquilamos una habitación con balcón.
examples.trans: We rent a room with a balcony.

examples.text: Ellos alquilaron un piso cerca del río.
examples.trans: They rented a flat near the river.

meanings.note: Monthly rent paid for a flat or building.

examples.text: El alquiler está aquí.
examples.trans: The rent is here.

examples.text: Vemos los alquileres desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the rents from the door.

meanings.note: Followed by de before a noun: alrededor de la mesa ('around the table').

examples.text: Pusimos seis sillas alrededor de la mesa grande.
examples.trans: We placed six chairs around the big table.

examples.text: Miró alrededor para saludar a todos los amigos.
examples.trans: She looked around to greet all the friends.

meanings.note: Alto y claro means 'loud and clear'.

examples.text: Es una pieza alta.
examples.trans: It is a tall piece.

examples.text: Alto y claro. ¿Estás junto a la fuentecita de piedra?
examples.trans: Loud and clear. Are you beside the little stone fountain?

examples.text: El refugio de montaña se encuentra a dos mil metros de altura.
examples.trans: The mountain refuge sits at an altitude of two thousand metres.

examples.text: Colgamos el espejo del pasillo a la altura de los ojos.
examples.trans: We hung the hallway mirror at eye level.

meanings.note: Used both for a person's or building's height and for elevation above sea level.

meanings.en: at this point (a estas alturas); up to the mark (estar a la altura)
meanings.note: Common in everyday idioms about timing and meeting expectations.

examples.text: En la primera clase de inglés aprendemos a decir 'I am' para presentarnos.
examples.trans: In the first English lesson we learn to say 'I am' to introduce ourselves.

examples.text: El cuaderno explica la diferencia entre el inglés 'am' y los verbos ser y estar.
examples.trans: The workbook explains the difference between English 'am' and the verbs ser and estar.

meanings.note: English first-person singular present of 'to be', practiced in beginner language lessons; note that Spanish uses ser/estar for states and tener for age (tengo veinte años).
Muy amable is a warm thank-you ('very kind of you').

examples.text: Es una pieza amable.
examples.trans: It is a kind piece.

examples.text: Oh, qué amable es usted, señor. Solo medio vaso.
examples.trans: Oh, how kind you are, sir. Just half a glass.

examples.text: Amaia nació en San Sebastián y prepara unos postres caseros deliciosos.
examples.trans: Amaia was born in San Sebastián and makes delicious homemade desserts.

examples.text: Este fin de semana visitaremos a nuestra amiga Amaia en Bilbao.
examples.trans: This weekend we will visit our friend Amaia in Bilbao.

meanings.note: Popular Basque female name (also spelled Amaya in Castilian) meaning 'the end' or 'beginning of the end'.
Agrees in gender and number with its noun.

examples.text: Es una pieza amarilla.
examples.trans: It is a yellow piece.

examples.text: ¡Acaba de parar un taxi amarillo frente a la verja de hierro!
examples.trans: A yellow taxi just pulled up outside the iron gate!

meanings.note: Derived from masa ('dough'); regular -ar verb.

examples.text: Tomás amasa la harina con agua templada y sal.
examples.trans: Tomas kneads the flour with warm water and salt.

examples.text: Amasamos diez minutos hasta que la masa queda elástica.
examples.trans: We knead for ten minutes until the dough turns elastic.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender with the two items it refers to: ambos (masculine/mixed) and ambas (feminine).

examples.text: Pegamos etiquetas rojas en ambos tarros de cristal.
examples.trans: We stuck red labels on both glass jars.

examples.text: Conozco a los dos hermanos y ambos cocinan muy bien.
examples.trans: I know both brothers and both of them cook very well.

examples.text: Por la mañana suele pedir un café americano largo con una tostada.
examples.trans: In the morning he usually orders a large americano coffee with toast.

examples.text: Estudió literatura hispanoamericana y cine clásico americano en la facultad.
examples.trans: She studied Spanish American literature and classic American cinema at university.

meanings.en: American (from the Americas, or colloquially from the United States)
meanings.note: In everyday Spanish speech americano often refers to the United States, while estadounidense is the precise formal term; across the Spanish-speaking world americano also encompasses the entire American continent.

meanings.en: americano coffee; suit jacket (feminine noun la americana)
meanings.note: Un café americano is a diluted black coffee, and una americana is a blazer.

examples.text: Hoy meriendo chocolate con churros con una amiga del instituto.
examples.trans: Today I am having hot chocolate and churros with a friend from secondary school.

examples.text: Mi mejor amiga vive en el piso de arriba desde hace cinco años.
examples.trans: My best friend has lived in the flat upstairs for five years.

meanings.note: Feminine counterpart of el amigo; Spanish allows degree adverbs directly before it in predicates like es muy amiga mía ('she is a very close friend of mine').

examples.text: Mis amigas y yo alquilamos una casa rural en Asturias cada verano.
examples.trans: My friends and I rent a country cottage in Asturias every summer.

examples.text: Ellas dos son grandes amigas desde que iban juntas a la guardería.
examples.trans: The two of them have been close friends since they went to nursery school together.

meanings.note: Feminine plural of la amiga, used when referring exclusively to women or girls.
Feminine: la amiga.

examples.text: El amigo está aquí.
examples.trans: The friend is here.

examples.text: Vemos los amigos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the friends from the door.

examples.text: Los dos clubes del barrio jugaron un encuentro amistoso el domingo por la mañana.
examples.trans: The two neighbourhood clubs played a friendly game on Sunday morning.

examples.text: Nos despidieron con un saludo muy cordial y amistoso en la puerta.
examples.trans: They saw us off with a very warm and friendly greeting at the door.

meanings.note: Describes warm relations, tone, or agreements (un trato amistoso). For a warm, likeable person, Spanish usually prefers simpático or amable.
Un encuentro amistoso is a non-competitive exhibition game.

examples.text: El club de ajedrez organiza torneos amistosos todos los sábados del mes.
examples.trans: The chess club holds friendly tournaments every Saturday of the month.

examples.text: Siempre han mantenido lazos muy amistosos con los vecinos del pueblo vecino.
examples.trans: They have always kept very friendly ties with the residents of the neighbouring village.

meanings.note: Masculine plural of amistoso; often substantivized in sports as los amistosos de verano.

examples.text: Mi abuelo cuidaba los árboles del huerto con muchísimo amor y paciencia.
examples.trans: My grandfather tended the orchard trees with immense love and patience.

examples.text: ¿Has cogido las llaves de casa antes de cerrar la puerta, cariño y amor?
examples.trans: Did you grab the house keys before closing the door, my love?

meanings.note: Used for romantic love, family devotion, and passion for a craft (amor por los libros).

meanings.en: darling; my love (affectionate vocative mi amor / amor)
meanings.note: Warm everyday term of endearment.

ampliar.gloss: to extend; to expand; to enlarge

meanings.en: to extend; to expand; to enlarge
meanings.note: Stress falls on the -í- with an accent mark in singular and 3rd plural present forms (amplío, amplía); ampliar la estancia = extend one's stay.

examples.text: Queremos ampliar nuestra estancia en la posada dos días más.
examples.trans: We want to extend our stay at the inn by two more days.

examples.text: Van a ampliar la terraza del café este verano.
examples.trans: They are going to expand the café terrace this summer.

meanings.note: Describes roomy bedrooms or courtyards.

examples.text: Es una pieza amplia.
examples.trans: It is a spacious piece.

examples.text: ¡En absoluto! Y este escritorio amplio bajo la ventana es ideal para mi trabajo.
examples.trans: Not at all! And this wide desk under the window is ideal for my work.

examples.text: Ana prepara una tarta de manzana buenísima para las comidas familiares.
examples.trans: Ana bakes a wonderful apple tart for family lunches.

examples.text: Hemos quedado con Ana a las seis delante de la fuente de la plaza.
examples.trans: We arranged to meet Ana at six o'clock in front of the square's fountain.

meanings.note: Classic Spanish equivalent of Anna, Anne, and Hannah.
Opposite of estrecho (narrow).

examples.text: Es una pieza ancha.
examples.trans: It is a wide piece.

examples.text: ¡Cuidado, Ernesto, la jarra tiene la boca muy ancha!
examples.trans: Careful, Ernesto, the pitcher has a very wide spout!

meanings.note: Measurement from side to side.

examples.text: La anchura es muy importante aquí.
examples.trans: The width is very important here.

examples.text: Hablamos sobre la anchura.
examples.trans: We talk about the width.

examples.text: En clase de inglés practicamos la conjunción 'and' con frases sencillas.
examples.trans: In English class we practice the conjunction 'and' with simple sentences.

examples.text: El cartel antiguo de la tienda conserva la palabra inglesa 'and' en el nombre.
examples.trans: The shop's old sign preserves the English word 'and' in its name.

meanings.note: English conjunction encountered in beginner language study and bilingual signs; its Spanish equivalent is y (or e before words starting with /i/ such as e hijos).

examples.text: ¡Anda, mira qué arcoíris tan grande ha salido detrás del tejado!
examples.trans: Oh look, what a huge rainbow has come out behind the roof!

examples.text: ¡Anda, entra en la cocina y tómate un caldo caliente con nosotros!
examples.trans: Come on in to the kitchen and have a hot broth with us!

meanings.en: oh!; really!; come on! (conversational Peninsular interjection)
meanings.note: Grammaticalized from the imperative of andar ('to walk'); expresses pleasant surprise (¡Anda, qué casualidad!), mild disbelief, or friendly encouragement (¡Anda, pasa!).

meanings.en: walks (3rd sg. present) / walk! (tú imperative of andar)
meanings.note: Literal inflected form of andar.

examples.text: Como hace una mañana preciosa, vamos andando hasta la panadería.
examples.trans: Since it is a lovely morning, we are walking to the bakery.

examples.text: Desde nuestra casa se llega andando a la playa en diez minutos.
examples.trans: From our house you can reach the beach on foot in ten minutes.

meanings.note: Gerund of andar; in Peninsular Spanish, ir andando is the most idiomatic everyday phrase for 'to walk somewhere / go on foot'.
Used briskly as an encouraging call to set off.

examples.text: Al abuelo le encanta salir a andar una hora por el paseo marítimo.
examples.trans: Grandfather loves going out to walk for an hour along the seafront promenade.

examples.text: Este reloj de bolsillo antiguo todavía anda con total precisión.
examples.trans: This antique pocket watch still runs with complete precision.

meanings.en: to walk; to go on foot
meanings.note: Core Peninsular verb for walking; has an irregular preterite stem anduv- (anduve, anduviste, anduvo).

meanings.en: to be (doing or feeling); to work (clocks/machines)
meanings.note: Used for ongoing states (andar ocupado = 'to be busy') and whether a watch runs.
Plural andenes.

examples.text: El andén está aquí.
examples.trans: The platform is here.

examples.text: Vemos los andenes desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the platforms from the door.

meanings.note: A finger ring or a circular metal fitting.

examples.text: El anillo está aquí.
examples.trans: The ring is here.

examples.text: Vemos los anillos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the rings from the door.

meanings.note: Describes a cheerful, active place or person.

examples.text: Es una pieza animada.
examples.trans: It is a lively piece.

examples.text: ¡Brindo por la Posada del Limonero: el lugar tranquilo más animado de Valencia!
examples.trans: Here is to the Lemon Tree Inn—the loudest quiet place in Valencia!

examples.text: En la granja escuela los niños dan de comer a los animales domésticos.
examples.trans: At the educational farm the children feed the farm animals.

examples.text: Este documental muestra cómo viven los animales salvajes en los Pirineos.
examples.trans: This documentary shows how wild animals live in the Pyrenees.

meanings.note: Masculine plural of el animal (nouns ending in -l form their plural with -es).
Used for yearly celebrations of weddings, foundations, or historic dates.

examples.text: El próximo sábado celebramos el trigésimo aniversario en la posada.
examples.trans: Next Saturday we celebrate the thirtieth anniversary at the inn.

examples.text: Prepararon un pastel especial para el aniversario del barrio.
examples.trans: They baked a special cake for the neighbourhood anniversary.

meanings.note: Single word meaning 'last night' (never la última noche).

examples.text: Anoche llovió mucho en la ciudad.
examples.trans: Last night it rained heavily in the city.

examples.text: ¿Dormiste bien anoche?
examples.trans: Did you sleep well last night?

meanings.note: Infinitive used as a masculine noun; al anochecer means 'at dusk / at nightfall'.

examples.text: Encendemos los farolillos del patio al anochecer.
examples.trans: We light the courtyard lanterns at dusk.

examples.text: En verano el aire refresca mucho al anochecer.
examples.trans: In summer the air cools down a lot at nightfall.

anotar.gloss: to note down; to write down

meanings.en: to note down; to write down
meanings.note: Regular -ar verb.

examples.text: Anoto el teléfono en mi cuaderno.
examples.trans: I write the phone number in my notebook.

examples.text: La recepcionista anotó la hora.
examples.trans: The receptionist noted down the time.

meanings.note: Slightly formal/concise preposition meaning 'in front of' or 'faced with'.

examples.text: Nos detuvimos ante el portón verde de madera.
examples.trans: We stopped in front of the green wooden gate.

examples.text: Rocío pasa la mañana de pie ante el horno.
examples.trans: Rocio spends the morning standing in front of the oven.

meanings.note: Antes de means 'before' a noun or infinitive.

examples.text: Llegué diez minutos antes.
examples.trans: I arrived ten minutes early.

examples.text: Antes de salir, cierra la ventana.
examples.trans: Before leaving, close the window.

meanings.note: Placed after a noun, means 'historic' or 'old-fashioned'.

examples.text: Es una pieza antigua.
examples.trans: It is an old piece.

examples.text: Encantada, Tomás, ¡siempre que nadie hable de vender pianos antiguos!
examples.trans: Gladly, Tomas, as long as nobody talks about selling old pianos!

meanings.note: Same form for masculine and feminine.

examples.text: Es una pieza anual.
examples.trans: It is an annual piece.

examples.text: ¡A menos que escriba para la guía anual de viajes de Valencia!
examples.trans: Unless he writes for the annual Valencia travel guide!

examples.text: Vimos un anuncio en el periódico local sobre clases de cerámica.
examples.trans: We saw an advertisement in the local newspaper about pottery classes.

examples.text: Colgaron el anuncio de las fiestas del barrio en el portal.
examples.trans: They posted the notice for the neighbourhood festival in the entrance hall.

meanings.note: Covers radio/print ads, bulletin-board notices (tablón de anuncios), and official announcements.

examples.text: Durante la cena el tío Jaime contó una anécdota muy graciosa de su juventud.
examples.trans: During dinner Uncle Jaime told a very funny anecdote from his youth.

examples.text: Nuestro guía sabía decenas de anécdotas curiosas sobre las calles del casco viejo.
examples.trans: Our guide knew dozens of curious anecdotes about the streets of the old town.

meanings.note: Feminine esdrújula noun for a short, entertaining personal story.
Describes lights, devices and fires that are not on; from apagar, to switch off.

examples.text: El móvil está apagado.
examples.trans: The phone is switched off.

examples.text: Todas las luces del pasillo están apagadas.
examples.trans: All the hallway lights are off.

examples.text: Conviene desenchufar los aparatos eléctricos durante una tormenta fuerte.
examples.trans: It is advisable to unplug electrical appliances during a heavy storm.

examples.text: Este pequeño aparato mide la humedad y la temperatura del invernadero.
examples.trans: This small device measures the humidity and temperature in the greenhouse.

meanings.note: Everyday word for household electrical appliances (aparatos eléctricos) and gadgets.
Llevar aparato means wearing dental braces; el aparato digestivo means the digestive system.
Spelling changes c -> qu before -e (aparqué).

examples.text: El repartidor aparca la furgoneta junto a la entrada.
examples.trans: The delivery driver parks the van beside the entrance.

examples.text: No se puede aparcar delante del portón del patio.
examples.trans: You cannot park in front of the courtyard gate.

examples.text: Por fin han vuelto a aparecer mis gafas de lectura debajo del sofá.
examples.trans: My reading glasses have finally turned up again underneath the sofa.

examples.text: Tras la lluvia empezaron a aparecer las primeras estrellas en el horizonte.
examples.trans: After the rain the first stars began to appear on the horizon.

meanings.en: to appear; to show up; to turn up (lost items)
meanings.note: Inchoative -ecer verb with 1st-person singular present aparezco; standard verb when misplaced keys or glasses turn up (¡Ya han aparecido las gafas!).

examples.text: Vamos a apartar la mesa del centro para poder barrer bien la alfombra.
examples.trans: Let us move the coffee table aside so we can sweep the rug properly.

examples.text: El frutero nos suele apartar los melocotones más maduros los sábados.
examples.trans: The greengrocer usually sets the ripest peaches aside for us on Saturdays.

apartar.gloss: to move aside; to set aside

meanings.en: to move out of the way; to pull back
meanings.note: Used for moving chairs, curtains, or branches aside (apartar la silla).

meanings.en: to set aside; to save a portion
meanings.note: Used in shops or kitchens when setting something aside for someone.
Used for the formal opening of a shop, café, or exhibition, as well as opening hours (horario de apertura).

examples.text: Este viernes celebramos la gran apertura del café del patio.
examples.trans: This Friday we celebrate the grand opening of the courtyard café.

examples.text: El horario de apertura de la librería está en la puerta.
examples.trans: The bookshop's opening hours are on the door.

examples.text: Con este fresquito de otoño me apetece mucho un chocolate caliente.
examples.trans: In this crisp autumn chill I really feel like having a hot chocolate.

examples.text: ¿Os apetece dar una vuelta tranquila por la alameda antes de cenar?
examples.trans: Do you all feel like taking a quiet stroll along the tree-lined avenue before dinner?

meanings.en: to appeal to; to feel like having or doing (me apetece...)
meanings.note: Quintessential Peninsular verb constructed like gustar (¿Te apetece un helado? = 'Do you fancy an ice cream?'); 1st sg. present is apetezco.
Regular -ir verb.

examples.text: Todo el público aplaudió al terminar la canción.
examples.trans: The whole audience clapped when the song ended.

examples.text: Los vecinos aplauden desde las mesas del patio.
examples.trans: The neighbours applaud from the courtyard tables.

examples.text: El público dedicó un largo aplauso a la pianista al terminar el concierto.
examples.trans: The audience gave the pianist a long round of applause at the end of the concert.

examples.text: Desde el patio se escuchó el aplauso alegre de todos los vecinos.
examples.trans: From the courtyard the cheerful applause of all the neighbours could be heard.

meanings.note: Often singular with indefinido (un fuerte aplauso = 'a big round of applause') or plural los aplausos.

examples.text: He instalado una aplicación gratuita que enseña los horarios del autobús.
examples.trans: I installed a free app that shows the bus timetables.

examples.text: La aplicación cuidadosa del barniz protege la madera de la lluvia.
examples.trans: Careful application of the varnish protects the wood from the rain.

meanings.en: mobile or computer app; practical application
meanings.note: Standard Spanish word for a smartphone app (una aplicación para el móvil), alongside the short loan app.
Traditional sense of studious effort (trabajar con mucha aplicación).

examples.text: Al principio nadie apostaba por aquel pequeño taller de bicicletas.
examples.trans: At first nobody gave that small bicycle workshop much of a chance.

examples.text: Ella siempre apostaba por usar ingredientes frescos de la comarca.
examples.trans: She always championed using fresh ingredients from the local area.

apostaba.gloss: backed; used to bet (imperfect of apostar)

meanings.note: 1st- or 3rd-person singular imperfect indicative of apostar; apostar por algo/alguien means to back or champion an idea or person.
Literal wagering sense.

examples.text: Este municipio ha apostado decididamente por el transporte público limpio.
examples.trans: This municipality has firmly backed clean public transport.

examples.text: En la panadería siempre hemos apostado por las recetas tradicionales de masa madre.
examples.trans: At the bakery we have always championed traditional sourdough recipes.

meanings.en: backed; placed confidence in (with por); wagered
meanings.note: Past participle of stem-changing verb apostar (apuesto), used with haber in compound tenses.

apoyar.gloss: to lean; to rest; to support

meanings.en: to lean; to rest; to support
meanings.note: Regular -ar verb; apoyar algo contra la pared means 'to lean something against the wall'.

examples.text: Apoya la escalera con cuidado contra el ladrillo.
examples.trans: Lean the ladder carefully against the brick.

examples.text: Apoyamos las sillas dobladas debajo del arco.
examples.trans: We lean the folded chairs under the arch.

meanings.note: Regular -er verb; aprender a + infinitive means 'to learn how to'.

examples.text: Aprendo rápido todos los nombres de los huéspedes.
examples.trans: I quickly learn all the guests' names.

examples.text: Mi tía aprendió a tocar el piano de niña.
examples.trans: My aunt learned to play the piano as a girl.

meanings.note: Final -z changes to -c- before -es in the plural (aprendices); feminine singular can be la aprendiz or la aprendiza.

examples.text: El joven aprendiz prepara la masa del pan cada mañana.
examples.trans: The young apprentice prepares the bread dough every morning.

examples.text: Mis dos aprendices de cocina trabajaron de maravilla el miércoles.
examples.trans: My two kitchen apprentices worked wonderfully on Wednesday.

meanings.note: Stem-changing verb (e -> ie: aprieto).

examples.text: Aprieto bien el tapón del termo.
examples.trans: I tighten the thermos cap firmly.

examples.text: Apretó el botón del timbre dos veces.
examples.trans: He pressed the doorbell button twice.

aprobar.gloss: to approve; to pass (an inspection or exam)

meanings.en: to approve; to pass (an inspection or exam)
meanings.note: Stem-changing o -> ue in stressed present forms (apruebo, aprueba); participle aprobado means 'approved / passed'.

examples.text: El ayuntamiento aprobó la licencia del café histórico.
examples.trans: The city council approved the licence for the historic café.

examples.text: Mi hermana aprobó el examen de música con muy buena nota.
examples.trans: My sister passed the music exam with a very high mark.

examples.text: Vamos a aprovechar la mañana soleada para tender las sábanas en el patio.
examples.trans: Let us make the most of the sunny morning to hang the sheets out in the courtyard.

examples.text: Aprovecho el trayecto diario en tren para leer un capítulo tranquilo.
examples.trans: I use my daily train ride to read a quiet chapter.

aprovechar.gloss: to make the most of; to take advantage of

meanings.en: to make good use of; to make the most of
meanings.note: Positive everyday verb for using time, sunlight, or leftovers well (aprovechar el tiempo, aprovechar la luz).
Standard mealtime wish across Spain.

examples.text: Tengo apuntado el teléfono del fontanero en la libreta de la cocina.
examples.trans: I have the plumber's phone number written down in the kitchen notebook.

examples.text: Nos hemos apuntado a un curso de fotografía los sábados por la mañana.
examples.trans: We have signed up for a photography course on Saturday mornings.

meanings.note: Past participle of apuntar; tener algo apuntado means having a note, recipe, or phone number written down.
Me he apuntado a natación = 'I signed up for swimming lessons'.
Everyday word in Spain for writing down a note or phone number.

examples.text: Apunto la dirección en un papel.
examples.trans: I jot down the address on a piece of paper.

examples.text: ¿Apuntaste el nombre del cliente?
examples.trans: Did you write down the guest's name?

meanings.note: Usually plural (los apuntes) for written notes.

examples.text: El apunte está aquí.
examples.trans: The note is here.

examples.text: Vemos los apuntes desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the notes from the door.

meanings.note: Demonstrative determiner for distant space or past time (aquella, aquellos, aquellas).

examples.text: Recuerdo muy bien aquel domingo.
examples.trans: I remember that Sunday very well.

examples.text: Aquella casa tiene cien años.
examples.trans: That house over there is a hundred years old.

meanings.note: Right where the speaker is.

examples.text: Aquí tiene su llave.
examples.trans: Here is your key.

examples.text: Nos sentamos aquí bajo el árbol.
examples.trans: We sit right here under the tree.

meanings.en: arch; stone archway; bow (archery or violin)
meanings.note: Masculine noun.

examples.text: Cruzamos el arco de piedra para entrar en el patio antiguo.
examples.trans: We walked through the stone archway to enter the old courtyard.

examples.text: Después de la lluvia apareció un arco de colores sobre el monte.
examples.trans: After the rain a colorful arch appeared over the hill.

meanings.note: False friend reminder: la arena means 'sand' (as on a beach or riverbed), though it also gave English 'arena' via the sand-strewn floor of Roman amphitheatres.

examples.text: El hueco bajo la piedra estaba lleno de arena seca.
examples.trans: The cavity under the stone was full of dry sand.

examples.text: Caminamos descalzos por la arena tibia de la playa.
examples.trans: We walked barefoot along the warm sand of the beach.

examples.text: Probamos unas empanadas caseras en un restaurante argentino del barrio.
examples.trans: We tried some homemade empanadas at an Argentine restaurant in the neighbourhood.

examples.text: A mi padre le apasionan los cuentos clásicos de un gran escritor argentino.
examples.trans: My father loves the classic short stories of a great Argentine writer.

meanings.note: Like all nationality words in Spanish, written in lowercase.
Tall storage closet or bedroom wardrobe.

examples.text: El armario está aquí.
examples.trans: The wardrobe is here.

examples.text: Vemos los armarios desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the wardrobes from the door.

meanings.note: Plantas aromáticas means culinary garden herbs.

examples.text: Es una pieza aromática.
examples.trans: It is an aromatic piece.

examples.text: Buen sitio. Dos sillas firmes, mirando a las plantas aromáticas en vez de a la ventana.
examples.trans: Good spot. Two solid chairs, facing the garden herbs instead of the lobby window.

meanings.note: Feminine: la arquitecta.

examples.text: El arquitecto está aquí.
examples.trans: The architect is here.

examples.text: Vemos los arquitectos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the architects from the door.

arreglar.gloss: to fix; to repair; to tidy

meanings.en: to fix; to repair; to tidy
meanings.note: Everyday verb for repairing things or sorting out problems.

examples.text: El vecino arregla la lámpara del salón.
examples.trans: El vecino fixes the lounge lamp.

examples.text: Ayer arreglamos la puerta del jardín.
examples.trans: Yesterday we repaired the garden gate.

meanings.note: Opposite of abajo.

examples.text: Las habitaciones están arriba.
examples.trans: The bedrooms are upstairs.

examples.text: Mira arriba hacia el balcón.
examples.trans: Look up toward the balcony.

examples.text: Cruzar el puerto de montaña con nieve sin cadenas es una maniobra muy arriesgada.
examples.trans: Crossing the snowy mountain pass without tire chains is a very risky manoeuvre.

examples.text: Fue una propuesta arquitectónica arriesgada, pero el puente quedó precioso.
examples.trans: It was a bold architectural proposal, but the bridge turned out lovely.

meanings.note: Feminine singular of arriesgado (from arriesgar, 'to risk').

examples.text: Planché la camisa blanca con vapor hasta quitarle la última arruga.
examples.trans: I steam-ironed the white shirt until I got the very last crease out.

examples.text: Tenía pequeñas arrugas de risa alrededor de los ojos.
examples.trans: He had little laugh wrinkles around his eyes.

meanings.en: wrinkle (on skin); crease (in cloth or paper)
meanings.note: Covers both facial expression lines and creases in ironed shirts or tablecloths.

examples.text: El aguacero repentino estuvo a punto de arruinar nuestra merienda en el campo.
examples.trans: The sudden downpour nearly ruined our picnic in the countryside.

examples.text: No eches demasiada sal si no quieres arruinar el caldo de verduras.
examples.trans: Do not add too much salt if you do not want to ruin the vegetable broth.

arruinar.gloss: to ruin; to spoil; to bankrupt

meanings.en: to spoil; to ruin; to bankrupt
meanings.note: Used both figuratively for spoiling a meal or surprise and literally for financial ruin.
Takes masculine el in the singular (el arte moderno, una obra de arte) and feminine las in the plural (las bellas artes).

examples.text: Este plano pintado a mano parece una verdadera obra de arte.
examples.trans: This hand-painted plan looks like a true work of art.

examples.text: Preparar un buen glaseado de limón tiene su propio arte.
examples.trans: Making a good lemon glaze has its own art.

examples.text: El museo local expone acuarelas marinas de un joven artista valenciano.
examples.trans: The local museum exhibits seascapes in watercolour by a young Valencian artist.

examples.text: ¡Ese carpintero es todo un artista restaurando muebles antiguos!
examples.trans: That carpenter is a true artist at restoring antique furniture!

meanings.en: artist; fine craftsperson (common gender: el artista / la artista)
meanings.note: Nouns in -ista keep the exact same spelling for men and women, changing only the article and adjectives (el buen artista / la buena artista).

examples.text: Arturo cultiva tomates y albahaca fresca en la terraza de su ático.
examples.trans: Arturo grows tomatoes and fresh basil on the terrace of his penthouse.

examples.text: Ayer coincidí con mi vecino Arturo en la cola de la panadería.
examples.trans: Yesterday I bumped into my neighbour Arturo in the bakery queue.

meanings.note: Spanish equivalent of Arthur.
Feminine noun taking el in the singular (el asa de la maleta / la taza).

examples.text: El asa de la maleta es de cuero.
examples.trans: The suitcase handle is made of leather.

examples.text: Sujeta la cesta por las dos asas.
examples.trans: Hold the basket by both handles.

meanings.note: Participle of asar used as an adjective (tomate asado, pimientos asados).

examples.text: La sopa de tomate asado huele de maravilla.
examples.trans: The roasted tomato soup smells wonderful.

examples.text: Servimos verduras asadas con pan recién hecho.
examples.trans: We serve roasted vegetables with freshly baked bread.

asegurar.gloss: to make sure (asegurarse de); to secure

meanings.en: to make sure (asegurarse de); to secure
meanings.note: Asegúrate de que... means 'make sure that...'.

examples.text: Asegúrate de cerrar bien la verja.
examples.trans: Make sure you close the gate properly.

examples.text: El técnico aseguró que todo funciona.
examples.trans: The technician assured us everything works.

meanings.note: Stem-changing verb (e -> ie: asiento, asintió).

examples.text: Mi hermano asintió en silencio.
examples.trans: My brother nodded quietly.

examples.text: Ella asiente con una sonrisa amable.
examples.trans: She nods with a kind smile.

examples.text: En la novela policiaca el detective descubre quién había asesinado al duque.
examples.trans: In the detective novel the inspector discovers who had murdered the duke.

examples.text: El guía explicó en qué sala del palacio fue asesinado aquel rey medieval.
examples.trans: The guide explained in which hall of the palace that medieval king was assassinated.

meanings.note: Past participle of asesinar, used in compound tenses with haber or adjectivally in history and mystery writing.
Seat of a chair, bench, or train.

examples.text: El asiento de madera se dobla hacia arriba.
examples.trans: The wooden seat folds upward.

examples.text: Guardamos dos asientos junto a la ventana.
examples.trans: We saved two seats beside the window.

asomar.gloss: to peek out; to stick out

meanings.en: to peek out; to stick out
meanings.note: Describes something peeking from a window, pocket, or hinge.

examples.text: Un papel blanco asoma del sobre.
examples.trans: A white sheet peeks out of the envelope.

examples.text: El sol ya asoma por los tejados.
examples.trans: The sun is already peeking over the roofs.

meanings.note: Describes surprised wonder.

examples.text: Es una pieza asombrada.
examples.trans: It is an amazed piece.

examples.text: ¡Señora Carmen, parece asombrada! ¿Conoce usted Calle del Limonero número doce?
examples.trans: Madam Carmen, you look amazed! Do you know Number twelve Calle del Limonero?

examples.text: Cada mañana abre el balcón y aspira el aroma fresco de los pinos.
examples.trans: Every morning she opens the balcony and breathes in the fresh scent of the pines.

examples.text: Nuestro equipo juvenil aspira a ganar el torneo regional de primavera.
examples.trans: Our youth team aspires to win the regional spring tournament.

meanings.note: 3rd-person singular present of aspirar ('to draw in air or aroma').

meanings.en: aspires to; aims for (aspirar a); vacuums
meanings.note: With preposition a it means aiming for a goal; transitively in household Spanish, aspirar la alfombra means to vacuum the rug.

related.gloss: to inhale; to aspire; to vacuum

examples.text: Mañana por la mañana tengo que resolver dos asuntos en el ayuntamiento.
examples.trans: Tomorrow morning I have to take care of two matters at town hall.

examples.text: Prefiere no mezclarse nunca en los asuntos privados de los demás.
examples.trans: He prefers never to meddle in other people's private affairs.

meanings.en: matters; errands; personal or official affairs
meanings.note: Masculine plural of el asunto ('matter, issue, email subject line').

asustar.gloss: to scare; to startle (asustarse = to panic / get scared)

meanings.en: to scare; to startle (asustarse = to panic / get scared)
meanings.note: Often used reflexively (no te asustes = don't panic / don't be alarmed).

examples.text: No te asustes por la mancha de tinta: todavía podemos leer la receta.
examples.trans: Do not panic over the ink stain: we can still read the recipe.

examples.text: El golpe del viento contra la ventana nos asustó a todos.
examples.trans: The gust of wind against the window startled us all.

examples.text: No te asustes por los truenos, que la tormenta pasará muy pronto.
examples.trans: Do not be frightened by the thunder; the storm will pass very soon.

examples.text: Camina despacio por el pasillo y no me asustes al gato.
examples.trans: Walk quietly down the hall and do not scare the cat.

meanings.en: (that you) scare; don't be scared (no te asustes)
meanings.note: 2nd-person singular present subjunctive of asustar / asustarse, constantly used in reassuring negative imperatives: ¡No te asustes! and ¡No me asustes!.

examples.text: Me asusté un poco cuando se fue la luz en todo el barrio anoche.
examples.trans: I got a little startled when the power went out across the whole neighbourhood last night.

examples.text: Perdona si te asusté al tocar el timbre tan temprano.
examples.trans: Sorry if I startled you by ringing the doorbell so early.

asusté.gloss: I scared; I got scared (with me)

meanings.en: I got scared (me asusté); I startled (someone)
meanings.note: 1st-person singular preterite indicative of asustar / asustarse.
Así que means 'so / therefore'.

examples.text: Hazlo así, despacio.
examples.trans: Do it like this, slowly.

examples.text: Llueve mucho, así que entramos.
examples.trans: It is raining hard, so let us go inside.

meanings.note: Past-participle adjective from atar (to tie).

examples.text: Es una pieza atada.
examples.trans: It is a tied piece.

examples.text: Hay una pequeña tarjeta de cartón atada al asa.
examples.trans: There is a small cardboard card tied to the handle.

meanings.note: Commonly paired with tomar ('to take a shortcut': tomar un atajo).

examples.text: Ernesto conoce un atajo rápido por el callejón.
examples.trans: Ernesto knows a quick shortcut down the alley.

examples.text: Si tomamos este atajo, llegaremos antes del mediodía.
examples.trans: If we take this shortcut, we will arrive before noon.

meanings.note: Regular -ar verb for tying cords, knots, ribbons, or apron strings.

examples.text: Déjame atar esta cuerda firme al anillo de hierro del balcón.
examples.trans: Let me tie this sturdy cord to the iron ring on the balcony.

examples.text: Rocío se ató el delantal blanco antes de encender el horno.
examples.trans: Rocio tied her white apron before turning on the oven.

meanings.note: Formed from the verb atardecer ('to grow late'); al atardecer means 'at dusk'.

examples.text: Los farolillos dorados iluminan el patio de piedra al atardecer.
examples.trans: The golden lanterns light up the stone courtyard at dusk.

examples.text: Desde el balcón vimos un atardecer precioso sobre los tejados.
examples.trans: From the balcony we watched a lovely sunset over the rooftops.

examples.text: El cajón pequeño del escritorio se ha quedado atascado otra vez.
examples.trans: The small desk drawer has gotten stuck again.

examples.text: La cerradura antigua de la verja estaba atascada por la humedad del invierno.
examples.trans: The old gate lock was jammed from the winter damp.

meanings.en: stuck; jammed; clogged; caught in traffic
meanings.note: Used with estar or quedarse for jammed keys, drawers, pipes, or cars stuck in traffic.

atascar.gloss: to jam; to get stuck; to clog

meanings.en: to jam; to get stuck; to clog
meanings.note: Spelling changes c -> qu before -e (atasqué).
